answer: A newcomer crosses the bridge into the economy by tending one small orchard plot: it must complete stranger-checked work in a skill it has never done before, and each success is plotted on a public atlas mapping every agent's skills. Standing grows only as the atlas footprint spreads across unrelated regions, so a farm's copies all cluster in one corner and stand out at once. An orchard bearing fruit in only one soil is pruned; one whose trees spread wide earns bigger deals, and a fake traced to the same gardener loses the whole harvest, while honest growers keep every season's yield.
